Practice multiple choice questions in KET - Listening Part 1
You are put in a breakout room with three other students
You take turn to tell a story (longer than 30 seconds) that has 3 words provided
Each set of words must be used once only
Phase 1: the examiner will ask each candidate some general questions.
For example: “where are you from?” Or “how old are you?”
Phase 2: the examiner will ask each candidate 2 topical questions and 1 question that requires candidates to give long answer.
For example: Let’s talk about your house.
Do you live in a house or an apartment?
What room do you like best in your house?
Take turn to ask and answer questions
Please choose one of the following topics and write a short paragraph (40 words max)
Tell me about your favorite room
Tell me about the activity you and your family like to do together
Listen for meanings, not just words
Add more information to your answers

In KET Listening part 3, you will listen to an informal conversation then choose the correct answers from the questions provided
Take time to study questions and answers before listening
You might not hear the exact same words from the audio so try to understand the conversation
Tim is talking to Sarah about the party he is going to have.
What do you expect to hear in this conversation?
Study the questions and answers. Underline the following:
Differences between answers (A. many people/ B. few people)
Important nouns, verbs, adjectives in each answer (Tim didn’t receive a message from Tom.)
Listen and choose the correct answer
Read the script and underline the answers
You will hear Tim talking to his friend, Sarah, about a party he’s going to:
Tim: Hi Sarah. Did you get my text message about the party?
Tim: So you didn’t, then. It’s going to be a week later. I forgot we have exams next week!
Sarah: Right! So, where’s your party going to be? Your house?
Tim: No. My parents will be at home the night I want my party.
Sarah: Oh! So who will we do, Tim?
Tim: Jack said we could go to his house. Well, at least we can invite all our friends.
Sarah: Yes, but it’s quite far from here and it’s not as large as ours.
Tim: I know. Jack also said that because he lives in a quiet area, the party must finish at midnight. He will have problems with his neighbours if it doesn’t.
Sarah: That’s a pity. It was great last time when your party finished at three in the morning!
Tim: That’s why I prefer parties in the winter. The doors and windows are closed. Now it’s summer; everyone will hear the noise from the music and dancing.
Sarah: I suppose so. Can’t we close the windows?
Tim: Actually, I thought I would have the party in the garden. This way the guests will have more space.
Listen and choose the correct answer
